message.content:
At a pressure of about 10 kPa (≈ 0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  

This is a well‑known result from the water phase diagram: as pressure falls below atmospheric pressure, the solid–liquid equilibrium line shifts to lower temperatures, so water freezes at a temperature slightly below 0 °C. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is about –2 °C (≈ –3.6 °F).
